newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- NOV 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- NOV 25.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--The government is in favour of the merger of smaller banks in the market and sees two major state-run groups based on the National and Commercial banks. National Economy and Finance Minister Yannos Papandoniou says he wants to see three large banks at most by the time Greece enters economic and monetary union (EMU) in 2000.
--Imports of cheaper used cars from the European Union and a drastic fall in charges has new car dealers worried about sales.
--Local girl Irene Skliva became Greece's first-ever Miss World title-holder amongst protests and tear-gas against the competition in Bangalore.

--The finance ministry has prepared a list of 368 businesses, stores and other firms involved in tax evasion costing the state more than 55 billion drachmas, to be released to the public along with the budget. National Economy and Finance Minister Yannos Papandoniou says the release of the list will be the first step in containing tax evasion.
--"There are no margins for retreat," Papandoniou says. "If we miss the train (for EMU), in 2001 we lose (EU) funds, major projects and our shield in national issues."

--President of the Republic Costis Stephanopoulos publicly asserts his opposition to package deals on the Aegean-Cyprus, during a tour of Thrace. The delineation of the Aegean continental shelf is the only issue up for negotiation with Turkey, he says.

--Senior officials at the general accounting office believe new urgent taxes will have to be imposed mid-1997 if the country is to meet the targets set in the budget. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
